question.text: During Timur's conquest of Asia Minor, he defeated and captured the Ottoman Sultan Bayezid the Thunderbolt near this modern-day capital of Turkey, after which he used Bayezid as a footstool and kept his wife in a cage.
question.clue: Kızılay ] Square, named for a certain "Red Crescent," is in this city, which was once known as Angora.

swap.text: At Piacenza, Alexios I was calling for help against the "Seljuk" variety of these people, who were themselves a subset of their "Ghuzz" variety. A group of "Young" ones rebelled against Sultan Abdul Hamid II in 1908.
swap.clue: The "16 States" popularized by nationalists from this ethnic group include the Ghaznavids.

question.text: This pirate sailed the Barbary Coast with his brother Aruj before becoming an admiral in the Ottoman navy and defeating the Holy League at the Battle of Preveza. He shares his name with a Holy Roman Emperor killed in the Third Crusade.
question.clue: He met with Antonio Rincon to negotiate an alliance between his monarch and Francis I, but his force was defeated at the Battle of Preveza by an allied fleet assembled by Pope Paul III in 1538.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about a class of people often found in imperial courts.
swap.text: The Chief Black Eunuch was the guardian of the Ottoman Imperial one of these. Ibrahim the Mad had one, but supposedly drowned all of its members in the Bosporus.
swap.clue: Wives and concubines in Islamic kingdoms were often sequestered in these areas of the palace. They were also called seraglios.

question.leadin: ANZAC troops landed at their namesake cove in this battle, and later made another landing at Suvla.
question.text: Name this World War I battle, also known as the Dardanelles Campaign, that ended in an Ottoman victory over ANZAC forces.
question.clue: This World War I battle, a disaster planned by Winston Churchill, was fought largely by the ANZAC corps of Australians and New Zealanders. Mustafa Kemal gained fame defending Turkey here.

swap.text: The Safavids also fought numerous wars with the Ottomans to the west, who defeated them at the Battle of Chaldiran while under this sultan. This sultan was succeeded by Suleiman the Magnificent.
swap.clue: Another great victory was at Chaldiran where he turned back Ismail I and his Turkmen followers, the Kizilbash.

question.leadin: Ipek Calislar ("chah-lish-lahr") was tried for "insulting the memory" of this man after publishing a book that credits Latife Hanım with many of his achievements.
question.text: Name this founder of the Republic of Turkey whose government promoted "Women's Role Models" like beauty pageant winner Feriha Tevfik.
question.answerHtml: Kemal Atatürk [or Mustafa Kemal Pasha; or Mustafa Kemal Ataturk]
question.clue: This leader who successfully defended Gallipoli from invasion and later helped to found a republic, of which he served as the first president.

swap.text: This period of Ottoman reform began with the 1839 "Noble Edict of the Rose Chamber." The reforms of this period, whose name means "reorganization," eliminated millet courts.

question.text: The Great Turkish War was ended by this 1699 treaty, which elevated the Habsburgs to premier status in Europe and effectively started the Ottomans' period of decline.
question.answerHtml: Treaty of Karlowitz [or Peace of Karlowitz; or Treaty of Karlovci; or Peace of Karlovci]
question.clue: Its Russian portion was supplemented in the following year by a treaty which transferred Azov, and it exempted an area defined by the Tisza, Mures, and Danube rivers, the Banat of Temesvar, from one provision.

swap.leadin: Identify the following figures with whom Francis I of France engaged in variously successful diplomacy.
swap.text: Thanks to the efforts of Captain Polin, this ruler joined Francis in besieging the city of Nice, an effort possibly thwarted by the exposure of Catherine Segurane's buttocks. Francis later lent support to this man's efforts against Tahmasp I.
swap.answerHtml: Suleyman I [or Suleyman the Magnificent; or Suleyman the Lawgiver]
swap.clue: The Treaty of Amasya ended the last of his wars with the Safavids, while his European exploits included a victory over the teenaged Louis II of Hungary at the battle of Mohacs.

question.leadin: Identify these individuals involved in the Gallipoli campaign.
question.text: After Enver Pasha's disastrous defeat at Sarakamis, this German general took control of much of the Ottoman military and oversaw the defense at Gallipoli; he later lost at Megiddo.

swap.text: This Young Turk and general served as the Minister of War and de facto leader of the Ottoman Empire during the Balkan Wars and World War I. His blaming of Armenians after his loss at Sarikamish prompted a genocide.
swap.clue: He then led the coup of January 23 organized by the Committee of Union and Progress, after which he become Minister of War as part of a triumvirate with Talaat and Djemal.

question.text: The five smartest children from each of these Ottoman provinces would be selected to learn about vaccines and hajamat blood treatment. The Tanzimat Reforms replaced [emphasize] eyalets ["AY-uh-lets"] with these units, which were led by people like Muhammad Ali in Egypt.

swap.leadin: The Treaty of Sevres demilitarized it until 3 years later, when the Treaty of Lausanne gave the rights of this body of water back to Turkey.
swap.text: Name this narrow strait which connects the Sea of Marmara and the Aegean Sea, fought over several times in history.
swap.clue: In 1915 Winston Churchill arranged an attempt by Ian Hamilton to approach the contested site by land from its north.

question.text: Attempts to collect reparations from Germany had been suspended in 1932 after a conference at this city. A 1923 treaty here recognized the state of Turkey and was the final treaty ending World War I.
question.clue: The large Greek population still living in Anatolia after World War I was forcibly exchanged with Turks in Greece by the terms of a convention signed in this city during negotiations to replace the Treaty of Sevres ("SEV").

swap.text: The implementer of the Turkish surname law, Mustafa Kemal, took the surname Ataturk, while this "National Chief" who succeeded him took his surname from a town where he fought during the Greco-Turkish War.
swap.clue: This overall commander of Ottoman forces at Beersheba later received a surname drawn from the two 1921 battles where he forced invading Greeks to retreat. He was the successor of Ataturk as the second President of Turkey.

question.text: Many Portuguese Jews reached the Ottoman Empire thanks to the network of this wealthy Sephardic woman, who convinced Suleiman the Magnificent to offer protection to Jews in Ancona. Her nephew received the title Duke of Naxos from Selim II, whom he persuaded to take Cyprus from Venice.

swap.leadin: Description acceptable. An elaborate Surname("soor-nah-MEH") that depicts parading glassworkers was created to celebrate the 1582 circumcision of a holder of this title.
swap.text: Give this title, whose holders were raised in seclusion as part of the kafes("kah-FESS") system. Roxelana engineered the 1553 execution of a holder of this title.
swap.answerHtml: şehzade (“shay-zah-DEH”) [or shâhzâde (“shah-zah-DEH”); accept Ottoman crown prince or heir-apparent to the Ottoman Empire; prompt on crown prince or heir-apparent by asking “in which Empire?”; prompt on children of the Ottoman Sultan or children of the Ottoman Emperor; reject “Ottoman Sultan,” “Ottoman Emperor,” or “Ottoman Caliph”]

question.text: As with the various denominations of Christians in the empire, this system granted the Ottoman Jewish community much autonomy over their internal affairs.
question.clue: This system, which allowed religious minorities to live independently of Islamic law, was abolished by the Tanzimat reforms in an attempt to reduce nationalist tendencies.

swap.leadin: A claim about this event originated in the Annals of the Empire discussing the reign of Holy Roman Emperor Maximilian II.
swap.text: Voltaire claimed that "nothing is better known" than what event, where the great commander Dragut was killed by a cannonball while trying to cut off Fort St. Elmo from Fort St. Angelo?
swap.clue: This 1565 "Great Siege", during which Knights Hospitallers under the command of Jean de Vallette successfully held off a far superior Ottoman force.
